subject: Proper left truncation in camera trap distance sampling

messages.author: a87e2d1885c9a643
messages.subject: Proper left truncation in camera trap distance sampling
parts:
Hello everyone,

This time I have two pretty simple questions regarding the proper implementation of left truncation in camera trap distance sampling (CTDS). 

We have a dataset of semi-automatically generated observation distances with a minimum value of 1 m, therefore I decided to remove all the distance estimates that are exactly 1 m and only use the values of 1.1 m and more to fit the detection function on the unbinned data.

Now I am not sure about the following points:

1. I would normally use the right truncation distance as the ω parameter in the CTDS formula. Does this still hold true when left-truncation is used in addition or would you subtract the left truncation distance from the right truncation distance to obtain ω?

2. Animals beyond the right-truncation distance are not counted, but what about animal observations with distances that are equal to or smaller than the left-truncation distance (in our case all animals with an observation distance of exactly 1 m)? Are they also not considered for the nk parameter of the CTDS formula?

 Thanks and all the best,

 Maik

messages.author: 75e0b0abcbafbc7d
messages.subject: Re: [distance-sampling] Proper left truncation in camera trap distance sampling
parts:
Maik

The analysis of Maxwell's duikers presented by Howe et al. (2017) in their MEE paper employs both left and right truncation.

By definition, detections made at distances smaller than the left truncation distance and greater than the right truncation distance are excluded from the analysis, hence are not counted in the $n_k$ portion of Eqn (2) of Howe et al. (2017).

Because Eqn (2) is producing an estimate of animal density, we want the first portion of the denominator ($theta * w^2$) to be the area sampled by the cameras.  Therefore the value of $w$ should reflect both left and right truncation distances.

Recognise the Distance R package as well as the Distance for Windows software can perform these calculations for you.

http://examples.distancesampling.org/Distance-cameratraps/camera-distill.html
